metadata.name: casi_escrow
metadata.description: CASI Escrow Program — Flash and Beam payment escrow for Solana

instructions.name: approve_flash
docs: Streamer approves a Flash: full amount → streamer ATA.
Vault + EscrowState are closed; rent returned to viewer (the original
rent payer at `initialize_escrow`).

accounts.name: viewer
docs: the escrow's `viewer` field via `has_one`.

instructions.name: approve_flash_delegated
docs: Delegated Flash approval. Same effect as `approve_flash`, signed by
the session key.

instructions.name: cancel_escrow
docs: Viewer cancels a pending Flash or Beam before the streamer acts.
Full refund; vault + EscrowState closed; rent returned to viewer.

instructions.name: cancel_stale_pending
docs: Permissionless refund for a Pending escrow that has sat untouched past
`PENDING_TIMEOUT_SECS` since creation. Anyone can crank this.
The refund destination is forced to `viewer_ata` so a cranker cannot
redirect funds.

instructions.name: deny_flash
docs: Streamer denies a Flash: full refund to viewer.
Vault + EscrowState are closed; rent returned to viewer.

instructions.name: deny_flash_delegated
docs: Delegated Flash denial. Same effect as `deny_flash`, signed by the
session key.

instructions.name: initialize_config
docs: One-time deployment initializer. Sets the accepted token mint, the
per-escrow cap, and the admin key. Uses `init` (not `init_if_needed`)
so it can only succeed once — calling it a second time always fails
with AccountAlreadyInitialized, preventing re-initialization attacks.
`accepted_mint` is stored but not updatable after init. If a different
mint is ever required, deploy a new program. Immutability here prevents
an admin key compromise from switching the mint out from under live
escrows.
`max_escrow_amount` — 0 means no cap (unlimited). Updatable by admin
via `update_config` so it can be tightened or loosened for a capped
launch without redeploying.

accounts.name: config
docs: `init` (not `init_if_needed`) makes this instruction callable exactly
once. A second call always fails with AccountAlreadyInitialized.

accounts.name: accepted_mint
docs: The token mint that this deployment will accept for all escrows.
Passing it as a verified on-chain account (rather than a raw Pubkey arg)
means Anchor's InterfaceAccount deserialization confirms it is a real
mint before the handler runs — a typo in the address is caught
immediately rather than silently bricking the deployment forever.

accounts.name: program_data
docs: This program's ProgramData account, owned by the BPF Upgradeable Loader.
Required so the instruction handler can verify that `initializer` is the
current upgrade authority, preventing front-running between deploy and
the first `initialize_config` call.
to this program. Upgrade-authority check happens in the handler.

instructions.name: initialize_escrow
docs: Viewer locks tokens into a PDA-owned vault ATA.
* `escrow_id`       — 32-byte UUID; used as PDA seed and stored for signing.
* `amount`          — token micro-units (e.g. 6 decimals for USDC; 1 USDC = 1_000_000).
* `duration_secs`   — 0 for Flash, > 0 for Beam.
* `escrow_type_val` — 0 = Flash, 1 = Beam.
Gated by GlobalConfig: fails if paused, if the mint doesn't match the
configured accepted mint, or if the amount exceeds the per-escrow cap.

accounts.name: streamer
docs: Not required to sign or co-operate at booking time (a viewer can still
book instantly) — but must have a StreamerRegistry account (see
below), a one-time step any real CASI streamer completes during
wallet setup.

accounts.name: streamer_registry
docs: Proves `streamer` opted in to receiving CASI escrows at some point in
the past — see register_streamer. Anchor fails this account's
deserialization (AccountNotInitialized) if it's never been created,
which is exactly the gate this exists for: without it, `streamer`
above is a fully unchecked, unsigned pubkey of the CALLER's choosing,
so anyone could open Pending escrows "against" an address that never
signed up for CASI at all. See
docs/fable-security-review-2026-08-10.md Finding 4.

accounts.name: config
docs: Global config is read to enforce: not paused, correct mint, amount cap/floor.

accounts.name: usdc_mint
docs: Must equal `config.accepted_mint`. Enforced in the instruction body
rather than as an inline constraint so the error is `InvalidMint`
rather than a generic account mismatch.

instructions.name: register_streamer
docs: One-time on-chain registration proving a pubkey is a real, opted-in
CASI streamer. initialize_escrow requires this account to exist for
whatever `streamer` pubkey a viewer targets — see
docs/fable-security-review-2026-08-10.md Finding 4. This is a
one-time setup step (during wallet connect), NOT a per-booking
requirement: once registered, a viewer can still book that streamer
instantly with zero live participation from them at booking time.
`init_if_needed` makes re-calling (e.g. after a wallet reconnect) a
harmless no-op rather than an error.

instructions.name: revoke_delegate
docs: Streamer revokes their session-key delegate. The PDA closes and rent
refunds to the streamer.

instructions.name: set_delegate
docs: Install or rotate a session-key delegate for a streamer.
Re-calling overwrites the session_key / expires_at in-place (rotation).

instructions.name: settle_beam
docs: Beam settlement with pro-rata vesting.
* Before `duration` elapses: only `streamer` or `viewer` may call.
* After `duration` elapses: permissionless (anyone may crank).
Integer proration: vested = total × min(elapsed, duration) / duration.

instructions.name: settle_beam_delegated
docs: Session-key path for early-ending a Beam. Same pro-rata vesting math as
`settle_beam`, authorized via a delegate PDA instead of the streamer's
wallet.
Trust model: a compromised session key can force-settle at any elapsed
time, including elapsed=0 immediately after start_beam (0 USDC to
streamer, full refund to viewer). This matches what the streamer can do
with the wallet-signed path and is an accepted risk: the attacker gains
nothing (funds always go to the declared parties), and the damage is
bounded and recoverable via `revoke_delegate`. The elapsed=0 case is
intentionally allowed so a streamer can end a beam immediately if needed
(wrong viewer, wrong content) without a wallet popup.

instructions.name: start_beam
docs: Streamer starts a Beam: records `start_timestamp`, sets status → Active.

instructions.name: start_beam_delegated
docs: Session-key path for starting a Beam. Identical effect to `start_beam`
except the signer is a pre-authorized delegate instead of the streamer
themselves.

accounts.name: streamer
docs: below bind this key to both the delegate PDA seed and the escrow's
own `streamer` field, preventing cross-streamer abuse.

instructions.name: transfer_admin
docs: Admin-only: transfer admin rights to a new key.
Two-step is NOT enforced on-chain — the admin is responsible for
confirming the new address is correct before calling this. Setting
admin to `Pubkey::default()` (the zero address) is rejected because
it would permanently brick `update_config` and `transfer_admin`.

instructions.name: unregister_streamer
docs: Reverses register_streamer — closes the registry account, so new
escrows can no longer target this pubkey until it re-registers.
Escrows already open against it are completely unaffected (same
non-retroactive spirit as GlobalConfig's pause flag) — this only
gates NEW initialize_escrow calls.

instructions.name: update_config
docs: Admin-only: flip the pause flag and/or adjust the per-escrow cap.
Pause only gates `initialize_escrow` — new escrows cannot be created
while paused. Existing escrows are NOT affected: viewers and streamers
can always settle, cancel, or approve regardless of the pause state.
This prevents a pause from trapping funds.
`accepted_mint` is intentionally NOT updatable here. Changing the
accepted mint after escrows are live could create an inconsistency
between what was locked (old mint) and what downstream code expects
(new mint). Deploy a new program instead.

errors.name: InvalidAmount
errors.msg: Amount must be greater than zero

errors.name: InvalidDuration
errors.msg: Duration must be > 0 for Beam escrows

errors.name: FlashMustHaveZeroDuration
errors.msg: Flash escrows must have duration_secs == 0

errors.name: InvalidEscrowType
errors.msg: Invalid escrow type — expected 0 (Flash) or 1 (Beam)

errors.name: Unauthorized
errors.msg: Caller is not the authorized party for this escrow

errors.name: AlreadySettled
errors.msg: Escrow is not in Pending status

errors.name: NotActive
errors.msg: Escrow is not in Active status

errors.name: WrongEscrowType
errors.msg: This instruction requires a different escrow type

errors.name: MathOverflow
errors.msg: Arithmetic overflow or underflow

errors.name: UnsupportedVersion
errors.msg: Account layout version is not supported by this program

errors.name: InvalidExpiry
errors.msg: Delegate expiry must be in the future

errors.name: DelegateLifetimeExceedsMax
errors.msg: Delegate expiry exceeds the maximum allowed lifetime

errors.name: DelegateExpired
errors.msg: Delegate has expired — streamer must re-install

errors.name: PendingNotStale
errors.msg: Pending escrow has not yet passed the stale timeout

errors.name: ProtocolPaused
errors.msg: Protocol is paused — new escrows cannot be created

errors.name: InvalidMint
errors.msg: Token mint does not match the configured accepted mint

errors.name: AmountExceedsCap
errors.msg: Amount exceeds the per-escrow cap set in GlobalConfig

errors.name: InvalidAdmin
errors.msg: Admin address cannot be the zero address

errors.name: TransferHookNotAllowed
errors.msg: Token mint has a TransferHook extension — not accepted by this program

errors.name: AmountBelowMin
errors.msg: Amount is below the per-escrow minimum set in GlobalConfig

errors.name: InvalidCapFloor
errors.msg: min_escrow_amount cannot exceed max_escrow_amount

types.name: GlobalConfig
docs: One global config account per deployment, seeded by CONFIG_SEED.
Initialized once by the deployer; `accepted_mint` is immutable after that.

fields.name: accepted_mint
docs: The only token mint accepted by `initialize_escrow`. Immutable.

fields.name: paused
docs: When true, `initialize_escrow` is blocked. Existing escrows are unaffected.

fields.name: max_escrow_amount
docs: Per-escrow maximum in token micro-units. 0 = no cap.

fields.name: min_escrow_amount
docs: Per-escrow minimum in token micro-units. 0 = no floor.
Set to a value that makes ATA-rent griefing uneconomical
(e.g. 1_000_000 = 1 USDC at 6 decimals; each deny costs the
streamer ~0.002 SOL to init the viewer ATA).

types.name: StreamerRegistry
docs: One per streamer who's opted in to receiving CASI escrows. Existence
alone is the whole signal — initialize_escrow just needs this account to
deserialize successfully for whatever `streamer` pubkey is targeted.
